question: Can BERT be used for document ranking in a multi-stage pipeline (pointwise then pairwise) that lets one trade ranking quality against latency?
hypothesis: A pairwise BERT stage (duoBERT) on top of pointwise monoBERT adds effectiveness for a modest latency increase when candidate admission is controlled per stage.
contributions: Describe monoBERT, a pointwise BERT relevance classifier (from Nogueira and Cho 2019)
Integrate both in a multi-stage ranking architecture that trades quality for latency by controlling candidate admission
Show that pre-training on the target-task corpus beats out-of-domain pre-training

method.summary: Three-stage pipeline: H0 BM25 (Anserini) retrieves k0 candidates, H1 monoBERT scores each (query, doc) pair independently and keeps top k1, H2 duoBERT scores ordered pairs (q, di, dj) among the k1 and aggregates pairwise probabilities into one score per document. Evaluated on MS MARCO passage ranking and TREC CAR 2017, with ablations over k0, k1 and aggregation.

datasets.name: MS MARCO passage ranking
datasets.size: 8.8M passages from 3.6M web documents; ~500k relevant query-passage pairs and 400M non-relevant pairs in train; avg 55 words per passage
datasets.split: dev 6,980 queries (about 1 relevant doc each); blind eval 6,837 queries via leaderboard
datasets.source: Bajaj et al. 2018, Bing query logs
datasets.preprocessing: No query or doc needed truncation; batches built with equal relevant and non-relevant passages (non-relevant ~1000x more frequent)

datasets.name: TREC CAR 2017
datasets.split: folds 1-4 train (~3M queries), remaining fold validation (~700k); test = TREC 2017 CAR (2,254 queries)
datasets.source: Dietz et al. 2017; queries = article title + section title
datasets.preprocessing: Fine-tuning pairs from top 10 BM25 docs per query: 30M pairs (3M x 10). BERT pre-trained only on the half of Wikipedia in the CAR training set (1.1B words) to avoid test leakage. Evaluated with automatic annotations, not the sparse manual ones.

datasets.name: Pre-training: Wikipedia + Toronto Book + MS MARCO corpus
datasets.size: Wikipedia 2.5B words, Toronto Book 0.8B words, MS MARCO corpus 0.5B words

models.name: monoBERT
models.architecture: BERT cross-encoder, [CLS] vector into a single-layer network giving relevance probability; query as sentence A, doc as sentence B
models.init_from: BERT pre-trained on Wikipedia+Toronto Book (1M iterations); for TCP, further pre-trained 100k iterations on MS MARCO corpus

models.name: duoBERT
models.architecture: BERT with three segment types (query A, di B, dj C), [CLS] into single-layer network giving p_ij
models.context: 512 tokens: query 62, di 223, dj 223 tokens; <1% of docs truncated

training.objective: monoBERT: cross-entropy over relevant/non-relevant candidates (Eq 1). duoBERT: cross-entropy over pairs with exactly one relevant doc (Eq 2).
training.steps: 100k iterations fine-tuning (12.8M query-document pairs); 100k iterations target-corpus pre-training
training.compute: about 24 hours fine-tuning on one TPU v3; about 24 hours for 100k-iteration second pre-training on a TPU v3
training.wall_clock: ~24 h fine-tune; another three days (50M pairs) gave no dev gain

inference.samples: SAMPLE aggregation averaged over ten trials; otherwise single run
inference.retrieval: BM25 top-k0=1000 to monoBERT, top-k1=50 to duoBERT in base configuration

parameters.aggregation: SUM, BINARY (pij>0.5 count), MIN, MAX, SAMPLE (m=10..40 drawn without replacement)

other.latency: measured in inferences per query; ms latency said comparable between mono and duoBERT but not reported

metrics.name: MRR@10
metrics.definition: mean reciprocal rank of first relevant doc in top 10 (MS MARCO official)

metrics.name: inferences per query
metrics.definition: BERT forward passes per query, proxy for latency

eval.protocol: Single trained model per configuration; no seeds or significance tests; eval-set scores only for submitted conditions (leaderboard).

results.table: Table 1, rows Anserini (BM25) and + monoBERT, column Dev (18.7 -> 37.2; Eval 19.0 -> 36.5)

results.table: Table 1, row + monoBERT + duoBERT_SUM, column Eval (37.0); dev 38.2 vs 37.2

results.claim: monoBERT gives a 19.5 MAP jump over BM25 on TREC CAR.
results.setup: TREC 2017 CAR test (2,254 queries), automatic annotations, MAP; k0=1000, k1=50
results.quote: jump of 19.5 MAP points over the BM25

results.claim: duoBERT SUM or BINARY adds 2.1 MAP over monoBERT on TREC CAR (36.9), best known result at the time.
results.setup: TREC 2017 CAR test (2,254 queries), automatic annotations, MAP; k0=1000, k1=50

results.claim: Anserini BM25 recall@1000 is 85.7% on MS MARCO vs 81.5% for Microsoft's BM25.
duoBERT SUM needs an extra 50 x 49 BERT inferences per query on top of monoBERT.
results.note: 2450 is derived (50x49); the text prints 50 x 49

results.claim: With k0=1000 vs smaller k0, over half the monoBERT gain is achieved with about a fifth of the inferences (diminishing returns).
results.setup: monoBERT only, vary k0 in {50,200,500,1000}, MS MARCO and TREC CAR (Fig 2)
results.quote: achieve more than half the gain in effectiveness

results.claim: k1=20 with BINARY (MS MARCO) or SUM (TREC CAR) reaches near-maximum score with only about a 40% latency increase over monoBERT; k1=50 more than doubles inferences.
Exhaustive pairs from a smaller monoBERT top-k1 beat uniform SAMPLE from a larger candidate set at the same inference budget.
results.setup: duoBERT SAMPLE m in {10,20,30,40} averaged over ten trials vs SUM/BINARY (Fig 3)

results.claim: Training 3 more days (50M pairs) gave no dev improvement; fine-tune is 12.8M pairs, ~24 h on a TPU v3.

limits: BERT size (base/large), parameter count and BM25 parameters are not stated.
Latency is proxied by inferences per query; milliseconds are asserted comparable but not reported.
Single runs, no seeds or significance tests; eval-set numbers missing for most conditions to avoid probing the leaderboard.
Inputs limited to 512 tokens (a few sentences); long documents untested (MS MARCO document task named as future work).
TREC CAR scored on automatic annotations because manual judgments are too sparse; no TCP result there since pre-training corpus is already Wikipedia.
Authors note MAP gains on CAR are larger than MRR@10 gains on MS MARCO partly because of metric properties, not only model strength.
Stages are tuned separately; joint tuning and passing earlier-stage scores forward are future work.
Dated: MS MARCO leaderboard standings (Oct 2019) and 'first application of BERT to retrieval' claims.

terms.definition: pointwise BERT relevance classifier scoring each (query, candidate) independently
pairwise BERT estimating the probability that candidate di is more relevant than dj
